steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Context: The Spanish Armada of 1588 was the culmination of decades of growing tension between England and Spain. Philip II of Spain, the most powerful monarch in Europe, was motivated by a combination of religious, political, and economic grievances against Elizabeth I. The execution of Mary Queen of Scots in February 1587 gave Philip the final justification he needed. | Weaknesses of the Armada: Despite its size, the Armada had significant weaknesses: (1) the original commander, the Marquis of Santa Cruz, died in February 1588 and was replaced by Medina Sidonia, who had no naval experience; (2) Drake's raid on Cadiz (1587) had destroyed supplies and delayed the fleet; (3) many of the ships were armed merchant vessels, not purpose-built warships; (4) the Spanish ships were designed for

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Give two reasons why Philip II of Spain wanted to invade England. (4 marks) | Describe the key events of the Armada campaign from 19 July to 29 July 1588. (4 marks) | Explain why the fire ships were a turning point in the Armada campaign. (4 marks)
